rule: Ordinance 86-013 and Decree 86-310 include products prepared by drying. personalMailApplicability: The law covers food imports through the final consumer and does not restrict articles 11–12 to resale or business importers. Applying that general scope to this paid personal postal purchase is an inference. Domestic preparation/handling/storage for private consumption is excluded; importing purchased food is not that activity.

30 September independent food/conformity review: Recovered the complete final CNLEGIS law from the official PIC portal after detecting adoption/HCC placeholders in the earlier FAO copy. Final copy records parliamentary adoption on 7 and 13 December 2017, HCC decision 09-HCC/D3 of 31 January 2018, and presidential promulgation on 8 February 2018. Compared final articles 2, 3, 11, 12 and 66. permitFreeReason: Not compatible with the no-certificate constraint: final enacted Law 2017-048 article 12 requires origin food-safety certification, independently of the unresolved phytosanitary classification. Applying the unqualified imported-food rule to a private postal purchase is an explicit legal-scope inference; no import exemption follows from the domestic private-preparation exception. The decision is based on the foreign-authority document duty, not on ordinary arrival inspection or the separate market-placement certificate.
independentFoodConformityRule: Law 2017-048, promulgated 8 February 2018, article 12 requires every imported food to have documents certifying origin and food safety issued by the competent authority of the country of provenance. Article 11 separately requires prior authorization. Article 2 covers imported food through the final consumer; its private-use exclusions concern domestic primary production, domestic preparation, handling and storage, not importing purchased food. Article 66 expressly includes raw or processed plant foods for human consumption. Decree2018-592 articles38–43 corroborate incoming plant-food consignment controls: article40 calls for accompanying sanitary certificates, and article43 requires documentary checks of all consignments. These incoming-consignment provisions are distinguished from the decree’s earlier export-control chapters; final Law article12 remains decisive.
foodConformityAccessNotes: The decisive source is the downloaded final official PIC-hosted law, not the FAO draft with unfilled enactment metadata. The implementing decree is a CNLEGIS text mirrored by Lexxika; the final law independently establishes the origin-certificate duty. Decree2018-592 has both earlier export-control chapters and incoming-consignment provisions at articles38–43; only the latter corroborate the import finding, while Law article12 independently establishes it.

independentFoodConformityRule: Official MBS Gazette Government Notice 21/2016, Malawi Bureau of Standards (Quality Development Cess) (Revocation) Order, paragraphs 3–4 apply to every importer of listed products regardless of end use or purpose. Paragraph 8 requires every such importer to furnish Form QDCO to the Director General for entry in the MBS register; the First Schedule item 91 expressly lists tea. The Second Schedule application is separate from a customs declaration and makes a firm stamp/designation optional. The cess payment itself is not treated as a prohibited document requirement.
foodConformityAccessNotes: The exact official GN21/2016 PDF was downloaded and its operative paragraphs and schedules visually inspected. It bears the unusual title including Revocation but its body imposes the cess and registration and revokes the earlier order; it is not merely a repeal notice. The older catalogue/article URLs now return migrated-site content, so their indexed text is supporting context only.

rule: The 1976 Plant Phytosanitary (Import Restriction) Notice expressly extends vegetative material, seeds and fruit to dried, frozen and chilled goods, but excludes goods described as cooked, or pickled and imported in bottles or cans. The actual printed item 64 contains the awkward wording "and mentioned herein" and requires certificates; it must not be silently rewritten as "not mentioned". The tea entry names vegetative material and seeds, not finished retail sencha. For this steamed product, whether the cooking exception applies and how the container qualification operates remain unresolved. The 2025 WTO review confirms the 1974 rules as amended in 1976 remain the operative starting point.
personalMailApplicability: The retrieved business-registration/for-sale food-import provisions were not extended to the private end consumer. Final enacted operative wording and a personal-post implementation rule were not recovered.
remainingQuestion: Does manufactured steamed/dried sencha qualify as cooked material excluded from the Notice, and does the bottle/can qualification attach to cooked goods as well as pickled goods? What rule is applied to sealed retail pouches in private post?

Its section 30 importer registration is expressly for import/export businesses, and section 33 food-import requirements are framed around imports for sale within Sierra Leone. The text therefore does not establish a special certificate duty for this private purchaser. WTO2025 reports adoption and later enacted legislation references the food-safety Act, so an unavailable final copy must not be described as proof that no law was enacted. Current SLSB material describes arrival inspection/testing, not a verified separate pre-import certificate duty for private tea parcels.
foodConformityAccessNotes: The downloadable FAO/Parliament 2017 text is explicitly a Bill, not a verified final promulgated version. WTO2025 and the 2021 enacted cross-reference demonstrate that food-safety legislation exists, but do not establish an unqualified private-import document duty in the unavailable final text.

permitFreeReason: The ordinary low-value PVoC exemption route requires an authority letter/application, but regulation7 separately allows destination inspection when a CoC is absent, and regulation8(1) uses an ordinary ESW customs declaration. The retrieved law does not conclusively establish that this alternative requires a special letter or application for this personal postal parcel. Automatic ICC issuance and arrival inspection are not themselves excluded by the user constraint. The independent conformity review therefore narrows the question but does not establish no-document exclusion; the separate manufactured-tea phytosanitary classification also remains unresolved.
independentFoodConformityRule: US EAS 921:2019 Green tea—Specification is currently marked compulsory in the official UNBS catalogue. UNBS Inspection and Clearance of Imports Regulations 2022 apply to compulsory-standard imports and regulation 6 expressly covers trade and personal use. Schedule 1 Part 2 and regulations 5(2), 5(5)(a) exempt qualifying consignments up to FOB USD2,000 from pre-export verification; regulation 8(2)(i) requires an exemption letter for the regulation 5(5) route where applicable. Bureau Veritas government-programme datasheet revision 11.1 (July 2023), pages 1–2, expressly includes the low-value category and says exempt exporters/importers need a letter directly from UNBS or the relevant authority at clearance. The official UNBS e-portal notice effective 1 July 2025 manages PVoC exemption requests through online applications. However, regulation7 independently allows Part1 goods without a CoC to undergo destination inspection with applicable fees/surcharge; regulation8(1) uses a customs declaration and 8(2)(i) requires the exemption letter only where applicable. The full set of lawful routes cannot be reduced to the ordinary low-value exemption process.
foodConformityAccessNotes: Direct official UNBS 2022 PDF retrieval, including the alternate menus/16 path, returned HTTP403; the full law was not downloaded. Cited primary clauses were retrieved from the official PDF search index. The BV programme PDF was downloaded in full and corroborates the specific letter requirement, citing the 2022 rules and UNBS letter BO/PVOC/020 dated 9 March 2023. The official 2025 workflow and compulsory-standard entry were available in the search index. This limitation is recorded rather than claiming a full primary-PDF read. Regulation7 permits destination inspection of Part1 goods arriving without CoC, with fees/surcharge. Whether this supplies an alternative no-exemption-letter route for a low-value personal parcel is not expressly resolved by the retrieved provisions; the decision concerns the evidenced ordinary low-value exemption route and has been flagged for root review.
